rules.title: Mark all electrical equipment with manufacturer identification and durable required ratings
rules.intent: Ensure every piece of electrical equipment is traceable to a responsible organization and that ratings and hazard labels survive the installed environment.
evidence_required: Equipment schedules showing manufacturer and model for all electrical equipment
Listing labels or nameplate photos showing manufacturer identification and ratings
Specifications for field-applied caution/warning/danger labels (durability, non-handwritten)

rules.title: Provide and maintain working space about electrical equipment
rules.intent: Guarantee ready and safe access for operation and maintenance of energized equipment.
evidence_required: Electrical room plans with dimensioned working clearances at panelboards, switchboards, and MCCs
Elevations showing 6.5 ft headroom and dedicated equipment space
Reflected ceiling / lighting plan showing workspace illumination
Door swing and egress details for rooms with equipment rated 800 A or more

rules.title: Identify grounded conductors by an approved means, including by system where systems are mixed
rules.intent: Prevent misconnection of grounded (neutral) conductors by requiring consistent, distinguishable identification.
evidence_required: Conductor schedule or one-line diagram noting grounded conductor color coding by system
Panelboard identification posting or documentation of neutral identification method
Cable and conductor specifications showing insulation colors

rules.title: Identify insulated grounded conductors 6 AWG or smaller by a listed means
rules.intent: Small grounded conductors must be identifiable along their entire length so they are never mistaken for ungrounded conductors.
evidence_required: Wire and cable specifications listing insulation color for grounded conductors
Panel schedules or details indicating white/gray neutral identification
For MI cable or PV cable, termination marking details

rules.title: Permit continuous white outer finish as grounded conductor identification
rules.intent: Establish the continuous white outer finish as the primary identification means for small grounded conductors.
evidence_required: Conductor specification showing continuous white insulation for neutrals
Field inspection photos of installed grounded conductors

rules.title: Identify insulated grounded conductors 4 AWG or larger by finish, stripes, or encircling termination marking
rules.intent: Large grounded conductors may be re-identified at terminations, but the marking must fully encircle the conductor.
evidence_required: Feeder conductor schedule showing neutral identification method
Termination marking detail (tape/marking encircling conductor) for large neutrals

rules.title: Reserve white, gray, or triple-striped insulation for grounded conductors only
rules.intent: Prevent shock and miswiring by prohibiting use of grounded-conductor colors on ungrounded conductors except under controlled reidentification conditions.
evidence_required: Wiring legend showing color coding by conductor function
Details for reidentified cable-assembly conductors used in switch loops
Inspection notes confirming white/gray used only as grounded conductors

rules.title: Provide readily accessible AFCI protection for dwelling, dormitory, and guest-room 120 V branch circuits
rules.intent: Reduce fire risk from arcing faults on 15 A and 20 A, 120 V branch circuits in sleeping and living areas.
evidence_required: Panel schedules identifying AFCI-protected branch circuits
Floor plans mapping outlets in AFCI-required rooms to protected circuits
AFCI device listing/type (combination-type, branch/feeder + outlet type, etc.)
Fire alarm branch circuit wiring method detail where the exception is used

rules.title: Identify branch-circuit grounded and equipment grounding conductors
rules.intent: Carry Article 200 and 250.119 identification requirements into every branch circuit.
evidence_required: Branch circuit conductor legend (neutral white/gray, EGC green or bare)
Panel schedule cross-referencing circuit conductor identification

rules.title: Identify ungrounded branch-circuit conductors per system type
rules.intent: Route each ungrounded conductor identification requirement to the correct subsection for ac multi-voltage or dc systems.
evidence_required: One-line diagram showing all nominal voltage systems on the premises
Conductor color-code schedule by system

rules.title: Identify ungrounded conductors by phase and voltage class where multiple nominal voltage systems exist
rules.intent: Prevent cross-system wiring errors by marking every termination, connection, and splice point and posting the method at each panelboard.
evidence_required: Color-code schedule by phase and voltage class on drawings
Panelboard label detail showing posted identification method
Splice/termination marking specification

rules.title: Identify dc branch-circuit ungrounded conductors by polarity (red positive, black negative)
rules.intent: Ensure dc polarity is unambiguous at every termination on systems over 60 volts.
evidence_required: DC one-line diagram with polarity color code legend
Panelboard posting or documentation of dc identification method
Conductor marking specification (red/black finish, stripes, or imprint intervals)

rules.title: Install required GFCI protection in readily accessible locations
rules.intent: Provide personnel shock protection wherever 210.8(A) through (F) require it, with devices that can be reset without tools or ladders.
evidence_required: Floor plans locating GFCI devices (breaker or receptacle) and demonstrating ready accessibility
Panel schedules flagging GFCI-protected circuits
Dimensioned plans showing sink/tub distances used to trigger GFCI requirements

rules.title: GFCI-protect dwelling unit 125-250 V receptacles in specified locations
rules.intent: Protect occupants from ground faults at receptacles in wet, damp, grade-level, and service locations of dwellings.
evidence_required: Dwelling floor plans with receptacles keyed to GFCI protection in each listed location
Panel schedule showing GFCI breakers or device schedule showing GFCI receptacles
Kitchen/bath elevations showing countertop and sink receptacle locations

rules.title: GFCI-protect dwelling bathroom receptacles
rules.intent: Bathrooms present the highest shock exposure in dwellings; every qualifying receptacle there must be GFCI protected.
evidence_required: Bathroom plans/elevations showing receptacle locations
Device or panel schedule showing GFCI protection for bathroom receptacle circuits

rules.title: GFCI-protect dwelling outdoor receptacles
rules.intent: Outdoor receptacles are exposed to wet conditions and must have personnel GFCI protection, with a narrow allowance for dedicated de-icing circuits.
evidence_required: Site/exterior elevation plans locating outdoor receptacles
GFCI device or breaker schedule for outdoor circuits
For de-icing exception: dedicated circuit identification and 426.28 GFPE documentation

rules.title: GFCI-protect dwelling basement receptacles
rules.intent: Basements are at or below grade and often damp; receptacles there require GFCI protection except a dedicated alarm-system receptacle.
evidence_required: Basement floor plan with receptacle circuits and GFCI devices
Fire/burglar alarm power connection detail where the exception is used
Confirmation that a separate 210.52(G) receptacle is provided when the exception receptacle is used

rules.title: GFCI-protect bathroom receptacles in other than dwelling units
rules.intent: Extend bathroom GFCI protection to commercial and institutional occupancies for qualifying receptacle ratings.
evidence_required: Non-dwelling bathroom plans with receptacle circuits identified
Panel schedule showing GFCI protection for those circuits

rules.title: Identify feeder grounded, grounding, and ungrounded conductors
rules.intent: Apply the same identification discipline to feeders as to branch circuits, including multi-voltage-system and dc polarity marking.
evidence_required: Feeder schedule and one-line diagram with conductor identification legend
Feeder panelboard posting/documentation of identification method
For dc feeders over 60 V, polarity marking specification

rules.title: Permit feeder-level GFCI in lieu of downstream GFCI provisions
rules.intent: Allow a single readily accessible feeder GFCI to satisfy branch-circuit and temporary-wiring GFCI requirements it supplies.
evidence_required: One-line diagram showing feeder GFCI device location
Documentation mapping which 210.8/590.6(A) requirements are satisfied by the feeder GFCI

rules.title: Scope: NFPA 72 29.6.3(5) secondary power-supply provisions for dwelling smoke alarms
rules.intent: Flag that smoke alarms in dwelling units have secondary power-supply requirements in NFPA 72 that interact with AFCI-protected circuits under 210.12.
evidence_required: Smoke alarm power supply detail (primary branch circuit and battery/secondary supply)
Fire alarm/smoke alarm submittal referencing NFPA 72 compliance

rules.title: Scope: raceway metric designators and trade sizes are identification only
rules.intent: Clarify that conduit/tubing size limits in Chapter 3 articles are expressed by metric designator and trade size per 300.1(C), which do not represent actual dimensions.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule using standard trade sizes/metric designators
Raceway fill calculations referencing the designated sizes

rules.title: Restrict wiring in ducts, plenums, and other air-handling spaces to methods complying with 300.22
rules.intent: Limit combustible wiring materials in air-handling spaces so smoke and fire are not distributed through the air system.
evidence_required: Mechanical/electrical coordination plans identifying plenums and fabricated ducts
Wiring method and cable listing documentation for plenum spaces
Support-accessory (cable tie) listing data for plenum installations

rules.title: Mark conductors and cables in accordance with 310.8
rules.intent: Conductor surface marking per 310.8 is the anchor for identifying cable type, size, and ratings, including enclosed conductors of prewired assemblies.
evidence_required: Cable cut sheets showing surface marking (type, size, temperature rating)
Prewired assembly tags/labels identifying enclosed conductors
Field photos of installed cable markings

rules.title: Limit IMC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4
rules.intent: Keep intermediate metal conduit within the sizes for which it is manufactured and listed.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing IMC sizes
Raceway fill calculations for each IMC run

rules.title: Prohibit FMC in wet locations, hoistways, battery rooms, and other listed conditions
rules.intent: Flexible metal conduit lacks liquidtight and physical-damage protection and is barred from the seven listed conditions.
evidence_required: Wiring method schedule keyed to location types (wet/dry, hazardous, underground)
Elevator hoistway wiring details where FMC is used per 620.21(A)(1)
Site plan confirming no FMC in underground or embedded runs

rules.title: Limit FMC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4, with 3/8 permitted only for listed short applications
rules.intent: Restrict undersized flexible metal conduit to controlled short-length uses such as motor leads and luminaire taps.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing FMC sizes
Details for any 3/8 trade size FMC showing qualifying application and length limit
Luminaire tap connection details

rules.title: Secure FMC within 12 in. of terminations and support at intervals not exceeding 4.5 ft
rules.intent: Keep flexible metal conduit mechanically supported so terminations and conductors are not stressed.
evidence_required: Installation details showing FMC strap spacing and distances to boxes
Support hardware specifications (listed cable ties or straps)
Ceiling-space luminaire whip details where exceptions apply

rules.title: Limit LFMC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4, with 3/8 only as covered in 348.20(A)
rules.intent: Restrict liquidtight flexible metal conduit sizes to those manufactured and listed, mirroring FMC small-size allowances.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing LFMC sizes
Details for any 3/8 LFMC showing qualifying 348.20(A) application

rules.title: Use PVC conduit only in the locations permitted by 352.10(A) through (I)
rules.intent: Confine rigid PVC conduit to concealed, corrosive, wet, damp, exposed-identified, and underground applications for which it is suited.
evidence_required: Wiring method schedule mapping PVC use to permitted locations
Underground raceway plan and burial depth details
Schedule 80 or identified PVC specification where exposed to physical damage

rules.title: Limit PVC conduit to trade sizes 1/2 through 6
rules.intent: Keep rigid PVC conduit within manufactured/listed size range.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing PVC sizes
Raceway fill calculations for PVC runs

rules.title: Limit HDPE conduit to trade sizes 1/2 through 6
rules.intent: Keep high density polyethylene conduit within manufactured/listed size range.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing HDPE sizes
Underground duct bank details for HDPE runs

rules.title: Mark NUCC every 10 ft per 110.21 and identify enclosed conductors per 310.8
rules.intent: Ensure the factory conductor-in-conduit assembly and its enclosed conductors remain identifiable after installation.
evidence_required: NUCC product cut sheet showing marking intervals and content
Assembly end/reel tag identifying enclosed conductors
Field verification photos of installed markings

rules.title: Limit NUCC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4
rules.intent: Keep nonmetallic underground conduit with conductors within manufactured/listed size range.
evidence_required: Underground conduit schedule showing NUCC sizes
Bending radius verification per Table 354.24

rules.title: Limit RTRC to trade sizes 1/2 through 6
rules.intent: Keep reinforced thermosetting resin conduit within manufactured/listed size range.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing RTRC sizes
RTRC listing data (e.g., Type XW where exposed to damage)

rules.title: Mark LFNC every 2 ft with type designation and trade size per 110.21
rules.intent: Keep liquidtight flexible nonmetallic conduit identifiable by type (LFNC-A/B/C), size, and suitability, including prewired assemblies.
evidence_required: LFNC product cut sheet with marking content and interval
Direct burial/outdoor marking verification
Prewired assembly tag detail

rules.title: Scope: LFNC type designations (LFNC-A, LFNC-B, LFNC-C)
rules.intent: Definitional scope rule: LFNC construction types determine allowable applications and lengths cited in Articles 356 and 620.
evidence_required: LFNC product data identifying type designation
Elevator/escalator details where LFNC-B lengths over 6 ft rely on 356.2(2)

rules.title: Limit LFNC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4, with 3/8 only for motor leads or short luminaire/equipment taps
rules.intent: Restrict undersized LFNC to controlled applications with length limits.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing LFNC sizes
Details for 3/8 LFNC applications with length verification

rules.title: Limit FMT to trade sizes 1/2 through 3/4, with 3/8 only per 300.22(B)/(C) or short luminaire assemblies
rules.intent: Flexible metallic tubing is a small, limited-use raceway; sizes outside 1/2 to 3/4 are barred except narrow allowances.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing FMT sizes
Air-handling space wiring details where 3/8 FMT is used per 300.22(B)/(C)
Luminaire whip length verification for 3/8 FMT

rules.title: Limit ENT to trade sizes 1/2 through 2 1/2
rules.intent: Keep electrical nonmetallic tubing within manufactured/listed size range.
evidence_required: Conduit schedule showing ENT sizes
Building height/thermal barrier documentation supporting ENT use per 362.10

rules.title: Identify grounded fixture wire per 402.8
rules.intent: Fixture wires used as grounded conductors must carry the Article 402 identification so the grounded conductor is distinguishable within luminaire wiring.
evidence_required: Luminaire wiring diagrams showing grounded fixture wire identification
Fixture wire specifications (type and identification means)

rules.title: Limit luminaire tap connections in small flexible raceways to 6 ft per 410.117(C)
rules.intent: Luminaire tap conductors run in 3/8 flexible conduit or as listed assemblies must be kept short and are the only basis for reduced securing/support.
evidence_required: Luminaire whip/tap details showing length not exceeding 6 ft
Listed assembly documentation for prefabricated luminaire whips

rules.title: Scope: auxiliary equipment limitations for electric-discharge and LED lamps per 410.137
rules.intent: Flag that ballasts, drivers, and other auxiliary lamp equipment on branch circuits permitted by 210.6 are further limited by 410.137.
evidence_required: Luminaire and ballast/driver schedule with voltage ratings
Branch-circuit voltage documentation per 210.6

rules.title: Scope: connect screw shell lampholders to grounded conductors per 410.90
rules.intent: Screw shell lampholders on circuits with a grounded conductor must have the screw shell connected to the grounded conductor, protecting persons relamping.
evidence_required: Luminaire wiring diagrams showing screw shell connected to grounded conductor
Lampholder terminal identification per 200.10(C)

rules.title: GFCI-protect outlets supplying appliances specified in 422.5(A)
rules.intent: Appliances identified in 422.5(A) must have GFCI protection from either the appliance side (422.5(B)(3)-(B)(5)) or the outlet/branch-circuit side (422.5(B)(1) or (B)(2)).
evidence_required: Appliance schedule identifying 422.5(A) appliances
Panel schedule or device schedule showing GFCI protection for those outlets
Appliance listing data where appliance-integral GFCI (422.5(B)(3)-(B)(5)) is relied upon

rules.title: Scope: appliances specified in 422.5(A) trigger GFCI requirements
rules.intent: The 422.5(A) appliance list (including vending machines per (A)(5) and dishwashers) defines which appliance outlets require GFCI protection.
evidence_required: Appliance schedule flagging 422.5(A) appliance types (e.g., vending machines, dishwashers)
GFCI protection mapping for each flagged appliance outlet

rules.title: GFCI-protect branch circuits supplying vending machines
rules.intent: Vending machines without appliance-integral GFCI must be supplied from GFCI-protected branch circuits.
evidence_required: Plans locating vending machine outlets
Panel schedule showing GFCI protection on vending machine branch circuits
Vending machine listing data if integral GFCI is claimed

rules.title: Scope: 422.5(B)(1) is an accepted supply-side GFCI means for appliance outlets
rules.intent: Identify GFCI provided in accordance with 422.5(B)(1) as one of the two supply-side compliance paths referenced by 210.8(D).
evidence_required: GFCI device schedule identifying the 422.5(B)(1) means used
Panel schedule cross-reference for the protected appliance circuit

rules.title: Scope: appliance-side GFCI per 422.5(B)(3) relieves the outlet GFCI requirement
rules.intent: Where GFCI protection is provided in accordance with 422.5(B)(3) (through (B)(5)), the supply outlet need not be separately GFCI protected.
evidence_required: Appliance listing/instruction data showing integral or factory-provided GFCI per 422.5(B)(3)
Submittal correlating appliance GFCI means to each affected outlet

rules.title: Apply 426.28 equipment ground-fault protection to dedicated de-icing/snow-melting receptacle circuits in lieu of GFCI
rules.intent: Dedicated snow-melting/de-icing circuits with not-readily-accessible receptacles may use 426.28 ground-fault protection of equipment instead of personnel GFCI.
evidence_required: Roof/site plan locating de-icing receptacles and demonstrating not-readily-accessible placement
Panel schedule showing dedicated circuit with equipment ground-fault protection
GFPE device specification per 426.28

rules.title: Scope: undersized raceway permitted only for enclosing motor leads per 430.245(B)
rules.intent: The recurring small-conduit exception (RMC, FMC, LFNC, EMT below trade size 1/2) exists solely to enclose motor terminal leads as permitted by 430.245(B).
evidence_required: Motor termination detail showing lead enclosure raceway type and size
Motor equipment submittal identifying factory lead arrangement

rules.title: Provide grounding-type, GFCI-protected receptacle outlets in mobile and manufactured homes
rules.intent: Mobile/manufactured home receptacles must be grounding type and carry GFCI protection per 210.8(A) plus the additional 550.13(B) areas.
evidence_required: Unit floor plan with receptacle layout and GFCI designations
Manufacturer wiring diagram showing grounding-type devices
Dielectric/continuity/polarity test records per 550.17

rules.title: Scope: GFCI requirements for boat hoists per 555.9
rules.intent: Flag that boat hoist outlets have dedicated GFCI requirements in Article 555 beyond the general 210.8 provisions.
evidence_required: Dock/boathouse electrical plan locating boat hoist circuits
GFCI device schedule for boat hoist outlets

rules.title: Use listed portable-type GFCI protection for cord-and-plug-connected temporary wiring
rules.intent: Temporary wiring GFCI protection supplied through plug-and-cord connection must be listed portable GFCI or equivalent so protection travels with the connection.
evidence_required: Temporary power plan identifying GFCI means for each circuit
Listing data for portable GFCI cord sets or devices
Assured equipment grounding conductor program documentation where used

rules.title: Restrict manufactured wiring systems to accessible dry locations and listed air-handling applications
rules.intent: Manufactured wiring systems are limited to accessible, dry locations unless listed for ducts/plenums and installed per 300.22, or listed for outdoor use.
evidence_required: Manufactured wiring system listing documentation
Reflected ceiling plan showing accessible installation locations
Plenum listing evidence where installed in air-handling spaces

rules.title: Use specified raceway or metal-clad cable wiring methods in elevator hoistways, machine rooms, and cars
rules.intent: Confine elevator, escalator, and lift wiring to robust raceway/cable methods, with flexible methods limited to 6 ft lengths except as specifically excepted.
evidence_required: Elevator electrical plans showing wiring methods in hoistway, car, and machine room
Details of flexible conduit lengths (6 ft limit) at controllers and machines
Class 2 cable support and protection details in hoistways
For OSHPD 1 projects, seismic switch hardwiring detail

rules.title: Supply other elevator utilization equipment from additional branch circuits with OCPDs in the machine/control room
rules.intent: Keep utilization equipment beyond car lighting, machine-room, and pit circuits on separate branch circuits with overcurrent devices located where elevator personnel can find them.
evidence_required: Elevator power riser/one-line showing separate branch circuits for other utilization equipment
Panel schedule locating overcurrent devices in machine/control room
Equipment list confirming loads fall within 620.1 scope

rules.title: Provide 110.26(A) working clearances at elevator controllers and disconnecting means
rules.intent: Elevator electrical equipment needs standard working space unless a qualified-persons condition of 620.5(A) through (D) is met.
evidence_required: Machine room / control space plans with dimensioned clearances at controllers and disconnects
Documentation of any 620.5(A)-(D) condition relied upon (flexible leads, guarding, low voltage)
Maintenance/supervision statement where clearance relief is claimed

rules.title: Identify solidly grounded PV system conductors at terminations per 200.6(A)
rules.intent: Single-conductor PV cable used as a solidly grounded conductor cannot rely on continuous white finish and must be marked at terminations at installation time.
evidence_required: PV system one-line diagram identifying grounded conductor configuration
Termination marking detail for PV grounded conductors
PV cable specification (single-conductor, sunlight-resistant, outdoor-rated)

rules.title: Supply PLFA circuits from listed power sources on dedicated, identified branch circuits without GFCI/AFCI
rules.intent: Power-limited fire alarm systems must have a listed power source and a dedicated, red-identified, qualified-access branch circuit that cannot be interrupted by GFCI or AFCI devices.
evidence_required: Fire alarm power source listing documentation (PLFA/Class 3)
Panel schedule showing dedicated fire alarm branch circuit without GFCI/AFCI
Fire alarm control unit label identifying the branch-circuit OCPD location
Red-identified disconnect detail marked FIRE ALARM CIRCUIT

rules.title: Supply NPLFA circuits at 600 V or less from Chapters 1-4 compliant sources on dedicated, identified branch circuits without GFCI/AFCI
rules.intent: Non-power-limited fire alarm circuits need a code-compliant power source not over 600 volts and a dedicated, red-identified branch circuit immune to GFCI/AFCI interruption.
evidence_required: Fire alarm power riser showing NPLFA source voltage (not more than 600 V nominal)
Panel schedule showing dedicated fire alarm branch circuit without GFCI/AFCI
Fire alarm control unit label identifying branch-circuit OCPD location
Red-identified disconnect detail marked FIRE ALARM CIRCUIT
